messages:
Elliot Price: Need quick alignment on public docs wording for Quantization Profile Library before we merge the beta page. Specifically: what we mean by “opt-in”, how we tell customers to evaluate quality, and how rollback should be described. Dropping proposed copy below 👇

Elliot Price: Proposed “opt-in” line: “Quantization profiles are off by default and only apply when you explicitly enable a profile on a specific route.”

Wei Chen: +1 on “off by default”, but we should be explicit that there’s no tenant-wide default in v1 (people will look for a global toggle).

Alex Martinez: Agree. Also please avoid phrasing that implies we automatically pick the best profile. This is a library + controls, not recommendations.

Monica Patel: Yep. In SDK examples we’re using `quantization_profile_ref` per route. If docs say “enable for your account” it’ll confuse.

Marissa Cole: Product POV: say “route-level opt-in” everywhere. And clarify you can scope by region/tier if configured, but still tied to the route config.

Paula Mendes: Telemetry note: we should set expectation that impact is measurable and customers should watch p95 + fallback_rate after enabling.

Elliot Price: Ok updated “opt-in” draft:

Elliot Price: “Quantization profiles are **route-level opt-in**. They are **disabled by default** and will not affect any traffic unless you explicitly set a `quantization_profile_ref` on a route (optionally scoped by region/deployment tier where supported).”

Wei Chen: That’s good. Maybe add one more sentence: “When disabled, Redwood serves the baseline (non-quantized) variant.”

Connor O'Brien: For rollback language, please don’t oversell “instant”. Config propagation isn’t instantaneous everywhere; it’s usually fast but we should say “typically within a few minutes” + “you can verify via headers/log fields”.

Dev Patel: From support: customers will ask “how do I know it applied?” If we can mention the `quant_profile_id` in logs/trace annotation, that’ll reduce tickets.

Elliot Price: Cool. For “how to evaluate quality”, I’m currently saying:

Elliot Price: “Before broad rollout, run an A/B evaluation on representative prompts and compare task-level metrics (accuracy, format adherence) and user-facing outcomes. Start with a small traffic percentage and expand gradually.”

Monica Patel: Could we be more prescriptive? Like “start with offline evals, then 1% canary” and mention that outputs can change even if overall quality is fine.

Marissa Cole: Yes, and we should say “quantization may change token-level outputs” (people interpret any diff as a bug).

Paula Mendes: Also call out metrics to watch: p95 latency, error rate, cost/token (if they have it), and fallback_rate. We should define fallback_rate in plain English.

Wei Chen: +1. “Fallback” will sound scary unless we define it as “served baseline because the selected profile is incompatible/unavailable.”

Naomi Feldman: For security/compliance wording: avoid implying we change model behavior silently. “Explicit customer action required” is the key phrase. Also mention audit logs / change history briefly (even if only a link).

Elliot Price: Draft section headers:
- What “opt-in” means
- How to evaluate quality
- Rollback and safety mechanisms

Elliot Price: Proposed “evaluate quality” block v2:
“Quantization can change outputs (including exact wording and formatting). Evaluate on your own prompt sets before expanding traffic:
1) Run offline comparisons on representative prompts (baseline vs profile-enabled) and review deltas.
2) Enable the profile on a single route and start with a small canary (e.g., 1–5%).
3) Monitor quality and production signals (p95 latency, error rate, fallback rate) and expand gradually.”

Alex Martinez: Looks good. Maybe add a sentence: “If your application requires strict structured output, validate schema/format adherence explicitly.” We keep seeing that.

Monica Patel: +1. And link to “structured output” docs if we have it.

Connor O'Brien: Rollback block should have two paths:
- Route-level disable (customer action)
- Platform kill-switch (Redwood action) for emergencies
But be careful: public docs should say “contact support” for kill-switch, not instruct them how to flip it.

Dev Patel: Yes please. We don’t want customers asking “where is the kill switch” in Console.

Wei Chen: Suggested rollback copy:
“Rollback is done by setting `quantization_profile_ref` back to `default` (or removing the field) on the route. Once disabled, traffic is served using the baseline precision. If you suspect an incident, disable the profile and contact Support with the route name, model, region, and a request ID.”

Paula Mendes: Add “verify recovery” steps: confirm fallback_rate returns to normal and latency normalizes, plus confirm in logs that `quant_profile_id` is empty/disabled.

Elliot Price: Adding “How to verify” bullet:
- Check route settings in Console change history
- Confirm request logs include `quant_profile_id` and resolution outcome (applied/fallback/disabled)

Alex Martinez: Wording nit: don’t say “empty” — say “disabled” or “not present”.

Elliot Price: Got it.

Naomi Feldman: Also add a short callout: “All changes are audited.” That satisfies a lot of enterprise questionnaires.

Marissa Cole: One more: clarify that “recommended/latest” aliases won’t auto-update under them in beta/GA docs unless that’s true. If we’re not shipping aliases as default behavior, keep docs on explicit profile IDs/versioned refs.

Wei Chen: Agree. For now, docs should bias to explicit versioned `profile_ref` and mention updates/deprecations in the library release notes.

Monica Patel: SDK examples are explicit refs, so consistent.

Elliot Price: Ok final proposed “opt-in” paragraph:
“Quantization profiles are **route-level opt-in**. They are **disabled by default** and will not affect any traffic unless you explicitly set a `quantization_profile_ref` for a route. When disabled, Redwood serves the baseline (non-quantized) precision. Quantization may change outputs; evaluate on your prompt sets before expanding traffic.”

Paula Mendes: +1 :thumbsup:

Connor O'Brien: +1, and for rollback add “typically takes effect within a few minutes” + “verify via logs.”

Dev Patel: +1. Please include the “contact Support with request ID” line.

Alex Martinez: +1. Can we also add a short “If you see unexpected behavior” troubleshooting list? (quality diffs vs latency regressions vs 5xx)

Elliot Price: I’ll add a small callout box:
- Output differences: run A/B on prompt set, check format adherence
- Latency regression: monitor p95, check fallback_rate, consider different profile
- Errors: disable profile + contact Support

Naomi Feldman: Works. Add “audit log / change history” link in that box.

Elliot Price: Cool. I’ll push these edits into the docs PR and tag @Alex @Monica for final review. If no objections by EOD, merging.

Wei Chen: Sounds good. Please also ensure we consistently use “quantization profile” vs “quant profile” in public docs.

Elliot Price: Will do. Thanks all.
